subject: Civil Engineering
title: Caissons: Building Underwater
description: A quick, practical guide to Caissons: Building Underwater.

hook.text: How do you dig a foundation at the bottom of a river? You send a box down.

buildup.text: A caisson is a watertight chamber sunk to the riverbed. Workers excavate inside.

discovery.text: Pneumatic caissons use compressed air to keep water out — workers breathe pressurized air.

twist.text: Rapid decompression caused 'the bends' — joint pain, paralysis, even death.

climax.text: Modern caissons use robotic excavation — no workers in pressurized chambers.

punchline.text: Sinking a box to bedrock is still the best way to start underwater.

quiz.question: What medical condition affected workers in pneumatic caissons?
options: Decompression sickness (the bends) from rapid pressure changes
Hearing loss from underwater noise levels
